blocks.heading: Committing to a secret
text: Nora restores synthesisers in Lisbon. Caleb collects them in Toronto. Neither will name a price first.
A hash breaks the deadlock without either of them saying a number.

blocks.heading: Monday morning, eighteen emails in
text: The Yamaha CS-30 is restored and listed at **€4,200**.
Nora will not go below **€3,900**. Caleb will not go above **€4,400**. There is a deal here worth €500 to whoever hears the other number first, so neither of them speaks.

blocks.heading: Send the fingerprint instead
text: Nora does not email her floor. She hashes it and emails the digest.

blocks.heading: Now neither of them can move
text: Caleb sends his own digest back the same hour. On Tuesday they both post the raw numbers.
Any lie is caught by re-hashing.

blocks.alt: Two digests posted on Monday, two revealed prices on Tuesday, and a re-hash step confirming each digest matches
blocks.caption: Nora learns Caleb's ceiling at the same instant he learns her floor.

blocks.title: Two properties, pulling opposite ways
text: **Hiding** - the digest tells Caleb nothing about the number.
**Binding** - Nora cannot open it as anything else later. Binding comes free from collision resistance. Hiding, as the next screen shows, does not come free at all.

blocks.question: Caleb sits on Nora's digest for a full day before he has to reveal anything. What can he do with it in that time?
answer: Guess. He knows the number is a price in euros, so it is not a random 256-bit value - it is one of a few thousand plausible ones.
He does not need to invert the hash. He only needs to hash every candidate and look for a match.

blocks.heading: The search is over before the kettle boils
text: Every whole-euro price from 1,000 to 9,999 is 9,000 candidates. One core, no optimisation:

blocks.label: tools/visuals/commitment.py

blocks.heading: The hash was never the weak part
text: SHA-256 held perfectly. It is still one-way, still avalanche-sensitive.
What failed is that the _input space_ was small and public. A pre-image is hard to find; a pre-image chosen from nine thousand obvious options is not.

blocks.heading: Nora adds sixteen hex digits
text: She generates 64 random bits, sticks them in front of the price, and hashes that. On Tuesday she reveals both.

blocks.heading: What that costs an attacker
text: The salt is not secret - Caleb gets it on Tuesday. Its only job is to make Monday's guessing useless.

blocks.caption: The same 9,000 prices, now hiding behind every possible salt.

blocks.heading: Where this still breaks
text: A commitment binds a value. It does not bind a person.

Caleb reveals €4,400. Nora reads it, decides she can do better, and simply never opens hers. Nothing in the mathematics compels her. Real protocols answer this with a deadline and a deposit she forfeits - a rule, not a proof.

blocks.heading: One sentence worth keeping
text: A hash hides a secret only as well as the secret is hard to guess; the salt is what buys the difficulty.
They settle at €4,150. Caleb wants to pay in bitcoin, and Nora's wallet is about to generate a number she will never look at.
